messages:
Mike H: Heads-up — I found a new invoice line: `accelerator_per_second_surcharge` for Feb. Looks like a per-second surcharge on G5 instances, total ~ $842.34. Anyone seen this before? link: https://billing.internal/redwood/invoices/2027-02 :eyes:
BillingBot: Automated alert: new charge type detected on account redwood-prod -> accelerator_per_second_surcharge (detected 2027-03-01T09:12Z). Suggested next step: tag reconciliation report. :robot_face:
Anya K: Uh — that sounds like the cloud provider started billing an extra fine-grained metering flag. Could be related to sustained use vs reserved offsets not applying. Where in the invoice does it map? region/sku?
Mike H: Snippet from the CSV (redacted):
```
line_item_id,service,sku,region,usage_type,amount
ln_987654,accelerator_per_second_surcharge,ACC-SURCH-G5,europe-west3,PerSecond,842.34
```
Anya K: Thanks. That SKU is new to our parsers. Our billing job maps `accelerator` -> accelerator_usage and `reservation` offsets. This looks like a separate surcharge SKU, so reservation offsets might not be matching automatically. :thinking_face:
Zoe L: I pulled recent deploys — we spun up a small fleet of g5.48x in europe-west3 last month for a large eval run, but those were on Dedicated (reserved capacity). Should have been covered by our commitment credits.
Ops Liaison: Did the Dedicated pools run under the same billing account? We have some Dedicated clusters billed to the infra-ops subaccount that should get committed discounts. If these nodes were launched in the main prod account accidentally, they'd be charged on on-demand rules.
Mike H: Good call. Tag on that CSV shows `project=research-eval` and `billing_account=redwood-prod` (not infra-ops). So hmm. Could be cross-account provisioning.
Anya K: Two hypotheses: 1) provider introduced a new surcharge SKU that isn't offset by our reservation credits (provider-side attribution change), 2) our Dedicated usage was billed to the wrong account (human error in provisioning). Either way we need to escalate to provider and also generate a reconciliation report.
Zoe L: I'll open a ticket with the provider support, include the invoice lines and our commitment contract IDs. Will ask them to confirm whether `ACC-SURCH-G5` should be eligible for reservation offsets. Ticket #{prov-4421}.
BillingBot: Added task: billing/reconcile/1812509876 assigned to Zoe L. Due 2027-03-03.
Mike H: For internal triage: can finance run a query for all `accelerator_per_second_surcharge` lines in last 6 months, grouped by billing_account and region? That will tell if it's isolated. @Anya K can you produce the quick query?
Anya K: Running now, will post CSV shortly. Expected columns: billing_account,region,amount,invoice_month,instance_tags.
Anya K: Quick summary: 2027-01: $0, 2027-02: $842.34 (single line, europe-west3, billing_account=redwood-prod), historical backfill shows $0 prior. So it's new and isolated to Feb.
Zoe L: Provider reply (summary): "This surcharge was added as of 2027-02-01 to account for per-second accelerator provisioning with new scheduler. Reservation offsets should apply if usage is tagged to the reservation contract. We see the usage reported under account `redwood-prod` and not `infra-ops` so offsets didn't apply." They asked for reservation contract IDs attached to usage to reprocess.
Mike H: That implies either our Dedicated agent mis-tagged or the provisioning path used the wrong account. Ops, can you confirm the infra agent version used for the eval run? We had a change in the agent last month that adjusted tags.
Ops Liaison: Confirmed: the eval run used agent v1.14.2 which had a tag bug (fix in v1.14.3) — it could drop `billing_account` tag on some pods. Deployments around 2027-02-10 are suspect. We already scheduled a patch but maybe it impacted a small subset.
Anya K: Action items: 1) reprocess invoice with provider attaching reservation IDs (Zoe), 2) run a retroactive tag reconciliation to reassign usage to infra-ops where appropriate (Finance + Ops), 3) update our invoice parser to treat `accelerator_per_second_surcharge` as reservation-eligible (DevEx).
Zoe L: Provider responded: they will reprocess if we provide a per-line mapping file. I'm prepping the CSV to include our reservation ID and original line_item_id. Expect submission by EOD.
Mike H: If provider accepts reprocess we should recover most of the $842.34 as a credit against March bill. If not, we need to book a one-off cost and update runbooks.
Anya K: Filed an internal postmortem placeholder: /docs/runbooks/billing/accelerator-surcharge-2027-02 (will fill root cause + mitigation).
Mike H: Thanks all. Let's keep thread for updates. :thumbsup:
